From this it is revealed that these two judgments have been set before God’s tribunal until the consummation of the world: one of these judgments has already been consummated in the flood by water, while the other will be consummated by fire.

“And there was a rainbow around the throne.” The rainbow around the throne has the same colors. The rainbow is called the bow, concerning which the Lord also spoke to Noah and his sons (Gen. 9), so that in God’s generation they would no longer fear a flood, but fire. For thus he says: “I shall set my bow in the clouds, so that you may no longer fear water, but fire.”

6. “And before the throne there was something like a glassy sea, like crystal.” That is, the gift of baptism, which he poured out through his Son [Col. 0324C] in the time of repentance, before he executes judgment. Therefore it is before the throne—that is, before judgment. But when he says “a glassy sea, like crystal,” he shows that the water was delivered as pure and stable, not agitated by wind, not flowing downward over a slope, but immovable like the house of God.

“And around the throne were four living creatures.” The four living creatures are the four Gospels.

7–10. “The first living creature was like a lion; the second like a calf; the third had a face like a human being; and the fourth was like a flying eagle. They had six wings, and all around and within they were full of eyes; and they had no rest, saying: ‘Holy, holy, holy, Lord Almighty.’ And the twenty-four elders fell down before the throne and worshiped God.” The twenty-four elders [Col. 0324D] are the twenty-four books of the prophets and the Law, which furnish testimonies concerning the judgment. They are also the twenty-four fathers: the twelve apostles and the twelve patriarchs.

The reason that the living creatures have different faces is this: the living creature like a lion designates Mark, in whom the voice of the lion roaring in the wilderness is heard. Matthew, however, strives through the human form to declare to us the lineage of Mary, from whom Christ received his flesh.

> **Note [Col. 0324D]: “Matthew strives through the human form to declare to us the lineage of Mary.”** Observe that he teaches that Matthew describes for us the genealogy of Mary, not of Christ, contrary to the opinion of the greater part of theologians today. [Col. 0325D]

Thus, when he enumerates from Abraham to David and down to Joseph, he speaks as though concerning a human being. [Col. 0325A] Therefore his proclamation presents the form of a human being. Luke, in recounting the priesthood of Zechariah as he offers a sacrifice for the people, and the angel appearing to him, assumed in his very composition the image of a calf, on account of the priesthood and the sacrifice. John the Evangelist, like an eagle, takes up wings, hastens to the heights, and discusses the Word of God.

Thus Mark the Evangelist begins: “The beginning of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, as it is written in Isaiah the prophet” (Mark 1:3): “The voice of one crying in the wilderness” (Isa. 40:3). He has the form of a lion. Matthew, however: “The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham” (Matt. 1:1); this is the face of a human being. Luke said: “There was a priest named Zechariah, of the division of Abijah, and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron” (Luke 1:5); this is the image of a calf. But John, when he begins, “In the beginning [Col. 0325B] was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God” (John 1:1), presents the likeness of a flying eagle.

The Evangelists not only express their four respective likenesses in the beginnings of their Gospels, but the Word himself of God the almighty Father, who is his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, bears the same images at the time of his advent. When he preaches to us, he is like a lion and a lion’s cub. When, for the salvation of human beings, he became a human being, it was to conquer death and free all. Because he offered himself as a sacrifice to the Father for us, he was called a calf. And because he conquered death and ascended into heaven, spreading his wings and protecting his people, he was named a flying eagle.

Therefore these proclamations, although they are four, are nevertheless one [Col. 0325C], because they proceeded from one mouth. Just as the river in paradise, though one, was divided into four parts. That the living creatures have eyes within and without in the proclamation of the New Testament signifies spiritual providence, which both examines the secrets of the heart and sees the things that are to come, which are within and without.

8. “Six wings.” They are the testimonies of the books of the Old Testament. Therefore twenty-four make the same number as the elders seated upon the judgment seats.

> **Note [Col. 0325D]: “Therefore twenty-four make the same number as the elders.”** In the manuscript the reading was: “Therefore twenty-four make so great a number as also the elders.” Even if this error must be believed to have originated not with the copyist but with the author himself, I nevertheless judged that, because it conflicts with correct expression, it should be removed by adding the adverb “the same number” and “as,” and changing the verb to “are.”

But just as a living creature cannot fly unless it has wings, so neither does the proclamation of the New Testament possess credibility unless it has the foretold testimonies of the Old Testament, by which it is lifted from the earth and flies. For whenever something is found to have been spoken beforehand and afterward fulfilled, that establishes an indubitable credibility. Conversely [Col. 0325D], if the wings do not adhere to the living creatures, they have no source from which to draw life. For unless the things foretold by the prophets had been fulfilled in Christ, their proclamation would have been empty. The catholic Church holds these things, which were both proclaimed beforehand and fulfilled afterward. And the living creature indeed flies, and deservedly is lifted from the earth.

The heretics, however, who do not employ prophetic testimony, also have the living creatures, but they do not fly, because they are earthly. The Jews, however, who do not accept the proclamation of the New Testament, have the wings, but do not fly—that is, they bring people an empty prophecy, since they do not compare the deeds with the words.

There are twenty-four books of the Old Testament that are received; you will find them in the *Epitomes of Theodore*.

> **Note [Col. 0325D]: “You will find them in the Epitomes of Theodore.”** This man’s writings have perished, like very many others. I have nothing certain to report to you about him, for chronological considerations prevent me from affirming that he was either Theodore of Heraclea or Theodore of Antioch. [Col. 0326D]

But the twenty-four elders also, as we have said—the patriarchs and the apostles—must judge their own people. For when the apostles asked and said, “We have left all that was ours and followed you; what then will there be for us?” (Matt. 19:27–28), [Col. 0326B] our Lord replied: “When the Son of Man sits upon the throne of his glory, you too will sit upon twelve judgment seats, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” And concerning the fathers who will judge, the patriarch Jacob also says: “Dan too will judge his people among his brothers, like one tribe in Israel” (Gen. 49:16).

5. “And from the throne proceeded flashes of lightning, voices, and peals of thunder, and seven burning torches of fire.” The flashes of lightning, voices, and peals of thunder proceeding from God’s throne, and the seven burning torches of fire, signify proclamations, promises of adoption, and threats. The flashes of lightning signify the coming of the Lord; the voices, the proclamations of the New Testament; the peals of thunder, that the words are heavenly; and the burning torches of fire, the gift of the Holy Spirit, which was rendered through the wood of the Passion.

And when these things took place, he says that all the elders fell down and worshiped the Lord, as the living creatures gave him glory and honor—that is, the Evangelical action, namely, and the teaching of the Lord [Col. 0326C]. When it had fulfilled the word foretold beforehand through them, they worthily and deservedly exult, aware that they had ministered the mysteries and the word of the Lord.

> **Note [Col. 0326D]: “That is, the Evangelical action and the teaching of the Lord.”** We think these words should be read in the accusative case, and that *Evangelia* (“the Gospels”) should be written in place of *Evangelica* (“Evangelical”). But each person will judge the matter according to his own discretion, for we are quite unable to discern what one is to understand from that construction of words.

Finally, because he had come who would dissolve death and alone was worthy to receive the crown of immortality, all possessed crowns as the glory of some excellent deed of their own.

10. “And they cast their crowns beneath his feet.” That is, because of the surpassing glory of Christ’s victory, they cast all their own victories beneath his feet.

> **Note [Col. 0326D]: “They cast all their own victories.”** We added the words “their own” and “they cast” ourselves. Moreover, where the text read *victoriam* (“victory”), which in our judgment made no sense, we restored *victoriae* (“of victory”). [Col. 0327D]

This is what the Holy Spirit fulfilled by showing it in the Gospel. For when our Lord, about to suffer at the end, came to Jerusalem and the [Col. 0326D] people went out to meet him, some cut down palm branches and spread them on the road, while others placed their tunics beneath him. They thereby represented two peoples: one of the patriarchs and the other [Col. 0327A] of the prophets—great men, namely, who cast beneath the feet of Christ, the conqueror of all, whatever palms of their own victories over sin they possessed. The palm and the crown signify the same thing, and they are given only to the victor.

## FROM CHAPTER V

1. “And I saw in the right hand of the one sitting upon the judgment seat a book written within and without, sealed with seven seals.” This book signifies the Old Testament, which was given into the hands of our Lord Jesus Christ, who received judgment from the Father.

2–3. “And I saw an angel full of might, proclaiming with a loud voice: ‘Who is worthy to open the book and loose its seals?’ And no one was found worthy, either in heaven or on earth or beneath the earth, to open [Col. 0327B] the book.” To open the book means to conquer death through a human being.

4. No one was found worthy to do this—neither among the angels in heaven, nor among human beings on earth, nor among the souls of the saints at rest—except Christ alone, the Son of God. John says that he saw him as a lamb standing as though slain, having seven horns. This had not been proclaimed at that time; and whatever the Law had prefigured concerning him through various offerings and sacrifices, he himself had to fulfill. And because he was the testator who had conquered death, it was right that he should be appointed the Lord’s heir, so that he might possess the substance of the one who dies—that is, the human members.

5. “Behold, the lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has conquered.” We read in Genesis that this lion of the tribe of Judah conquered, where the patriarch Jacob says: “Judah, your brothers will praise you. You have lain down, slept, and risen like a lion and like a lion’s cub” (Gen. 49:8–9). He is called a lion in relation to conquering death, but in relation to suffering for human beings, he was led like a lamb to the slaughter. Yet because he conquered death and forestalled the executioner’s office, he is described as though slain.

He therefore opens and unseals the testament that he himself had sealed. Moses the lawgiver signified this: because it had to remain sealed and concealed until the advent of his Passion, he veiled his face and thus spoke to the people, showing that the words of the proclamation were veiled until the coming of its appointed time. For when he himself had read to the people, he took scarlet wool, sprinkled the whole people with the blood of a calf and with water, and said: “This is the blood of his covenant, which has cleansed you” (Exod. 24:7–8).

> **Note [Col. 0327D]: “Scarlet.”** From Heb. 9:20 it appears that *coccinea* (“scarlet”) should be read instead of *succina* (“amber-colored”). —GALLAND.

It is therefore necessary to observe that the man preaches diligently and that all things cohere as one. For it is not enough that it be called a law; rather, it is named a testament. No law is called a testament, nor is anything else called a testament except what those about to die make. Whatever belongs to the inner contents of a testament is sealed until the day of the testator’s death.

Therefore it is now rightly unsealed by the slain Lamb, who like a lion [Col. 0328A] shattered death, fulfilled the things that had been foretold concerning him, and liberated the human being—that is, the flesh—from death, and took possession of the substance of the dying one—that is, the human members. Thus, just as through one body all human beings had fallen under the debt of their own death, through one body also all believers, reborn unto life, might rise again.

Rightly, therefore, the face of Moses is opened and unveiled; and for this reason the Apocalypse is called “Revelation.” For now Moses’ book is unsealed; now the sacrificial offerings are understood; now the preparation of the priests’ anointing oil is understood; and the testimonies too are understood openly.

8–9. “The twenty-four elders and the four living creatures, holding lyres and bowls and singing a new song.” The proclamation of the Old Testament joined with the New signifies the Christian people singing a new song [Col. 0328B]—that is, publicly presenting their confession. It is new that the Son of God becomes a human being. It is new that he ascends bodily into heaven. It is new that he grants human beings remission of sins. It is new that human beings are sealed with the Holy Spirit. It is new to receive the priesthood of sacred observance and to await the kingdom of the immeasurable promise.

The lyre—and its string stretched upon wood—signifies Christ’s flesh joined to the wood of the Passion. The bowl signifies confession and the succession of the new priesthood. The praise of the many angels—indeed, of all—is the salvation of all and the testimony of the whole creation rendering thanks to our Lord for the liberation of human beings from the calamity of death.

The unsealing of the seals, as we have said, is the opening of the Old Testament and the disclosure of things proclaimed as destined to occur [Col. 0328C] in the last time. Although the prophetic Scripture speaks of them under each individual seal, nevertheless, once all the seals are opened together, the proclamation possesses its proper order.

## FROM CHAPTER VI

1–2. “And when the Lamb had opened one of the seven seals, I saw and heard one of the four living creatures saying, ‘Come and see.’ And behold, a white horse, and the one sitting upon it had a bow.” When the first seal was opened, he says that he saw a white horse and a crowned rider holding a bow. For this was the first thing accomplished through him. After the Lord had ascended into heaven and opened all things, he sent the Holy Spirit, whose words the preachers discharged like arrows reaching [Col. 0328D] the human heart, so that they might conquer unbelief.

> **Note [Col. 0327D]: “Discharged.”** We added this word (*emiserunt*, “they discharged”) [Col. 0328D], and replaced *sagittae* (“arrows,” nominative) with *sagittas* (“arrows,” accusative). Surely anyone should regard this reading as better than that of the ancient manuscript, in which we do not place great confidence.

The crown upon the head, however, was promised to the preachers through the Holy Spirit. The other three horses more clearly signify the wars, famines, and plagues proclaimed by our Lord in the Gospel. Therefore he says that one of the living creatures said—for all four are one—“Come and see.” “Come” is said to one invited to faith; “see” is said to one who did not see. The white horse, therefore, is the word of proclamation sent into the world with the Holy Spirit. [Col. 0329A] For the Lord says: “This Gospel will be preached throughout the whole world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.”

3–4. “And when he had opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying, ‘Come and see.’ And another horse came forth, a red one, and a great sword was given to the one sitting upon it.” The red horse and the one sitting upon it with a sword signify future wars, as we read in the Gospel: “For nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be great earthquakes in various places” (Luke 21:10–11). This is the rose-colored horse.

5. “And when he had opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature saying, ‘Come and see.’ And behold, a black horse, and the one sitting upon it had a balance in his hand.” The black horse signifies famine, for the Lord says [Col. 0329B], “There will be famines in various places.” Properly, however, the saying extends as far as the times of the Antichrist, when there will be a great famine and when all will be harmed. The balance in his hand is the scale of examination, by which he would reveal the merits of each individual. He then says:

6. “Do not harm the wine and oil.” That is: do not strike the spiritual person with plagues. This is the black horse.

7–8. “And when he had opened the fourth seal, I heard the fourth living creature saying, ‘Come and see.’ And behold, a pale horse; and the name of the one sitting upon it was Death.” The pale horse and the one sitting upon it had the name Death. The Lord had likewise promised that these things would come among the other calamities: great plagues and mortalities. For he says:

“And hell followed him.” That is, it awaited [Col. 0329C] the devouring of many impious souls. This is the pale horse.

9. “And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw beneath the altar the souls of those who had been slain.” He relates that he saw the souls of the slain beneath God’s altar—that is, beneath the earth. For both heaven and earth are called an altar, just as the Law, commanding in a figurative representation of the truth that two altars be made [Col. 0329D], prescribed a golden altar within and a bronze altar without.

> **Note [Col. 0329D]: “Commanding that two altars be made.”** In place of this, the manuscript had the exceedingly corrupt reading—unless I am mistaken—“By the mediation of him who had made two altars.” Yet I shall not regard this emendation as so certain and established that, if someone demonstrates a better one, I would not abandon mine and approve the one he proposes.

We understand that heaven is thus called the golden altar, as our Lord bears witness to us. For he says: “When you offer your gift at the altar”—our gifts, assuredly, are the prayers we offer—“and there remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar” (Matt. 5:23–24). Prayers assuredly ascend to heaven. Heaven, therefore, is understood as the golden altar that was within. For the priests who had the anointing oil entered once a year to the golden altar, the Holy Spirit thereby signifying that Christ would do this once.

Just as the golden altar is recognized as heaven, [Col. 0330A] so the bronze altar is understood as the earth. Beneath it is hell, a region removed from punishments and fires, and the resting place of the saints. There the righteous are indeed seen and heard by the impious, but the latter cannot be conveyed across to them.

He who sees all things wished us to understand that these saints—that is, the souls of the slain—seek vengeance for their blood, that is, for their body, upon those dwelling on earth. But because in the last time the perpetual reward of the saints and the condemnation of the impious are both to come, they were told to wait. And for the consolation of their bodies, individual white robes were given to them. “They received,” he says, “white robes”—that is, the gift of the Holy Spirit.

12. “And I saw, when he had opened the sixth seal, that a great earthquake occurred.” The great earthquake that occurred under the sixth seal is that final persecution itself.

[Col. 0330B] “And the sun became black like a sack of haircloth.” The sun becomes like a sack—that is, the splendor of the teaching will be darkened for unbelievers.

“And the whole moon became like blood.” The blood-colored moon signifies that the Church of the saints sheds its blood for Christ.

13. “And the stars fell to the earth.” The falling of the stars signifies the faithful who are troubled for Christ.

“Just as a fig tree casts its unripe figs.” A shaken fig tree loses its unripe figs when people are separated from the Church by persecution.

14. “And heaven withdrew like a scroll being rolled up.” Heaven being rolled up means that the Church will be removed from the midst.

“And every mountain and the islands were moved from their places.” The mountain and the islands being moved from their places signify that in the final persecution [Col. 0330C] all have withdrawn from their places. That is, the good will be moved as they flee persecution.

## FROM CHAPTER VII
2. And I saw another angel ascending from the rising of the sun, having the seal of the living God. He means the prophet Elijah, who is to precede the times of Antichrist in order to restore the churches and strengthen them against the great and intolerable persecution. We read that these things were foretold in the opening of the book of the Old and New Testaments. For he says through Malachi: “Behold, I shall send you Elijah the Tishbite, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children” (Mal. 4:5–6)—that is, at the time of their calling, to recall the Jews to the faith of the people who follow. And therefore, as we have said, he reveals the number of those from the Jews who will believe, and from the Gentiles a great multitude which no one could number.

[Col. 0330D] We also read in the Gospel that the prayers of the Church are sent from heaven by the angel, and that they are received against the wrath, and that the kingdom of Antichrist is poured out and reckoned by the holy angels [the text is corrupt and its meaning uncertain]. For he says: “Pray that you may not enter into [Col. 0331A] temptation; for there will be great distress, such as has not been from the beginning of the world; and unless the Lord had shortened those days, no flesh would be saved” (Mark 13:18–20).

> **Note:** [Col. 0329D] *The prayers of the Church are also sent from heaven.* This passage is obscure, and we do not think it free from corruption. We wished, however, merely to note it, not to emend it, so that other religious scholars also might have an opportunity to exercise their ingenuity upon it. Yet we do not think we are making an inept conjecture if, instead of *illos*, we read *illas*, and instead of *aestimari*, *extingui*. If this further correction were added—namely, that the earlier conjunction *et* be placed after the word *Ecclesiae*—I do not see why that verbal construction, which at first was so obscure and corrupt, would not become much sounder and clearer. Whatever more diligent scholars may decide about it, if they offer some reason, we shall gladly follow.

Therefore he will send these seven great archangels to strike the kingdom of Antichrist. For he himself also spoke thus: “Then the Son of Man will send his messengers, [Col. 0331D] and they will gather his elect from the four corners of the wind, from the ends of heaven to its ends” (Mark 13:27).

> **Note:** [Col. 0331D] *Then the Son of Man will send his messengers.* All the authoritative passages cited both from the Old and from the New Testament are so corrupt and distorted—as anyone may see—that this Victorinus of ours, whoever he may have been, either knew no Greek at all or followed with excessive scrupulousness some edition that the Church was commonly using at that time. For what he shortly adds concerning the pit of Nimrod and the spirit of the Church presents no little difficulty and obscurity. Besides the fact that those words differ greatly from the Greek sources from which they were drawn, the subsequent order of the words also—unless we are mistaken—has been so corrupted that it is exceedingly difficult to extract the genuine sense from them. If, however, more learned scholars offer anything more consonant with reason, we shall readily subscribe to their judgment.

For previously he also said through the prophet: “Then there will be peace in our land, when seven shepherds and eight bites of men have risen up in it, and they will track Asshur”—that is, Antichrist—“in the pit of Nimrod” (Mic. 5:5–6), that is, in the nation of the devil, by the spirit of the Church. Likewise, “when the keepers of the house are shaken.”

The Lord himself, moreover, in the parable addressed to the apostles, when the laborers came to him and said, “Lord, [Col. 0331B] did you not sow good seed in your field? Whence, then, are there tares in it?” answered them: “An enemy has done this.” They said to him, “Do you wish us to go [Col. 0332D] and uproot it?” But he said: “No; rather, allow both to grow until the harvest, and at harvest time I shall tell the reapers to gather the tares and make them into bundles” (Matt. 13:27–30), and to burn them with eternal fire, but to gather the wheat into my barns.

> **Note:** [Col. 0332D] *Do you wish us to go?* Who does not see here that so little regard has been paid to Latin ears and elegance of expression that, if someone were to summon the author before a court and compel him to plead against the charge of having injured the dignity of the Latin language, he would not appear to have done so unjustly or rashly?

The Apocalypse therefore shows here that these reapers, shepherds, and laborers are angels. The trumpet, moreover, is the word of power. And although he repeats the matter through the bowls, it is not said as though it happened twice. Rather, because what the Lord has decreed to occur will happen once, it is therefore spoken of twice. What he said less fully under the trumpets is here in the bowls.

The order of the statements must not be regarded, because often, when the Holy Spirit has run forward to the end of the last times, he returns again to those same times and supplies what he stated less fully. Nor should an order be sought in the Apocalypse; instead, the meaning of the things prophesied must be followed. Thus the trumpets and bowls signify either the destruction caused by plagues sent upon the world, or the madness of Antichrist himself, or the falling away of peoples, or the diversity of the plagues, or hope in the kingdom of the saints, or the fall of cities, or the great fall of Babylon—that is, of the Roman city.

9. After these things I saw, and behold, a great multitude which no one could number, from every nation, tribe, people, and language, clothed in white robes. When he speaks of a great multitude from every tribe, he reveals the number of the elect from among all believers, who, purified through baptism in the blood of the Lamb, have made their robes white, preserving the grace [Col. 0331D] which they received.

## FROM CHAPTER VIII

1. And when he had opened the seventh seal, [Col. 0332A] there was silence in heaven for about half an hour. By this is signified the beginning of eternal rest. But he understood only a portion of it, because, after interrupting the silence, he repeats it in due course. For if the silence were perpetual, the narrative would end here.

13. And I saw one angel flying through the midst of heaven. By the angel flying through the midst of heaven the Holy Spirit is signified, bearing witness through the two prophets that the great wrath of the plagues is imminent—so that, if anyone should somehow be willing to be converted at the last time, someone might still be saved.

## FROM CHAPTER IX

13–14. And I heard one voice from the four horns of the golden altar which is in the sight of God, saying to the sixth angel who had the trumpet: “Release the four angels.” That [Col. 0332B] is, those holding the four winds at the four corners of the earth.

Who are bound at the great river Euphrates. By the corners of the earth, or the four winds beyond the river Euphrates, are meant four nations. For an angel has been assigned to every nation, as the Law says: “He established them according to the number of the angels of God” (Deut. 32:8), until the number of the saints is fulfilled. They do not pass beyond their appointed boundaries, because at the last time they will come with Antichrist.

## FROM CHAPTER X

1–2. I saw another mighty angel descending from heaven, clothed with a cloud; and there was a rainbow over his head, and his face was like the sun, and his feet like pillars of fire. And he had in his hand an open book, and he placed his right foot upon the sea, but his left upon the land. This mighty angel, whom he says [Col. 0332C] descended from heaven clothed with a cloud, signifies our Lord, as we explained above.

His face was like the sun. That is, because of the resurrection.

Over his head was a rainbow. This intimates the judgment which has been or will be carried out through him.

An open book. The revelation of deeds at the future judgment, or the Apocalypse which John received.

His feet. As we said above, these are the apostles. For the fact that both sea and land are trodden by him signifies that all things are subjected beneath his feet. He calls him an angel, that is, a messenger—namely, the messenger of the Father; for he is called the “Messenger of Great Counsel.” He also says that he cried out with a loud voice. The loud voice is the proclamation of the words of the heavenly and omnipotent God to humankind, solemnly testifying that, once the opportunity for repentance has been closed, there will afterward be no hope.

[Col. 0332D] 3. The seven thunders uttered their voices. The seven thunders uttering their voices are the Holy Spirit of sevenfold power, who through the prophets solemnly testified to all things that were to come; and John bore witness [Col. 0333A] in the world with his voice. But although he says that he was about to write down all that the thunders had spoken—that is, whatever had been obscurely foretold in the Old Testament—he is forbidden to write it. Instead, he must leave those things sealed, because he is an apostle, and it was not fitting for the grace belonging to the subsequent rank to be placed in the first. “The time,” he says, “is near” (Rev. 1:3; 22:10).

For the apostles overcame unbelief by powers, signs, wonders, and mighty works. After them, once those same churches had been brought to completion, the consolation of the prophetic Scriptures, which were afterward to be interpreted, was given—I mean the later interpreters as prophets [the wording is uncertain]. For the Apostle says: “And God has appointed in the Church, first apostles, second prophets, third teachers” (1 Cor. 12:28), and the rest. And elsewhere he says: “Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others judge” (1 Cor. [Col. 0333B] 14:29). And he says: “Every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head” (1 Cor. 11:5).

But when he says, “Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others judge,” he is not speaking of an unheard-of and unknown catholic prophecy, but of one both proclaimed and known. They are to judge whether the interpretation agrees with the testimonies of the prophetic utterance. It is therefore evident that this was not necessary for John, who had been armed with the superior power, since the body of Christ, which is the Church, adorned with its own members, ought to answer appropriately in its own place.

10. I took the book from the hand of the Angel, and ate it. To receive the book and eat it means to commit to memory the revelation made to him.

And it was in my mouth sweet as honey. Its sweetness in the mouth is the fruit of proclamation for the speaker, and is exceedingly sweet to the hearers; but for those who proclaim and persevere in the commandments, it is exceedingly bitter because of suffering.

11. And he says to me: “You must prophesy again to peoples, languages, nations, and many kings.” He says this because, when John saw these things, he was on the island of Patmos, condemned by the emperor Domitian to labor in the mines. There, therefore, he saw the Apocalypse. And when, already an old man, he thought that through suffering he would receive his final reception, Domitian was killed and all his judgments were annulled. John was released from the mines, and thus afterward handed down this same Apocalypse which he had received from God. This, therefore, is what he says: “You must preach again to all nations,” because you see the hosts of Antichrist rising up; the nations will take their stand against them, and each side will fall by the other’s sword.

## FROM CHAPTER XI

[Col. 0333D]

1. And there was shown to me a reed like a rod, and the angel stood, saying: “Rise and measure the temple of God and the altar, and those who worship in it.” A reed like a rod was shown: this is the Apocalypse itself, which he afterward presented to the churches; for he also later wrote the Gospel for the sake of our salvation in the perfect faith.

For when Valentinus, Cerinthus, Ebion, and the others of the school of Satan had spread throughout the world, all the bishops from the neighboring provinces assembled before him and compelled [Col. 0334A] him to compose his own testimony as well.

By the measure of the temple of God we mean the commandment of our Lord: to confess that the Father is almighty; that his Son, Christ, was begotten in the presence of the Father before the beginning of the age; that he became human with a true soul and flesh; that, after both misery and death had been conquered, he was received by the Father into heaven with his body; and that he poured out the Holy Spirit, the gift and pledge of immortality. He was proclaimed through the prophets, written of through the Law; he is the hand of God and the Word of the Father from God, in every respect the Lord and creator of the world. This is the reed and the measure of faith, and no one worships at the holy altar unless he confesses this faith.

> **Note:** [Col. 0333D] *The measure of the temple of God.* In place of this, the manuscript read “of the Son of God.” We changed it because it plainly seemed to contradict the words of the Apostle. [Col. 0334D]

2. Cast outside the court which is within the temple. An *aula* is called a court, an empty altar-space between walls. He commanded that such persons, as unnecessary, be cast out of the Church. [Col. 0334B]

It has been given to be trodden by the Gentiles. That is, by the people of this world, so that it may be trampled by the Gentiles, or together with the Gentiles. He then repeats the ruin and destruction of the last time, and says:

3. They will tread the holy city for forty-two months; and I shall give authority to my two witnesses, and they will preach for one thousand two hundred and sixty days, clothed in sackcloth. That is, three years and six months; these make forty-two months. Their preaching, therefore, lasts three years and six months, and the kingdom of Antichrist an equal length of time.

5. If anyone wishes to harm them, fire proceeds from their mouths and consumes their enemies. When he says that fire proceeds from the mouths of those prophets against their adversaries, he means the power of the word. For all the plagues, however many are to come, will be sent at their utterance by their angels.

Many think that Elisha, or else Moses, will be with Elijah; but both of them died. Elijah’s death, however, is nowhere found, and all our predecessors have handed down that the one with him is Jeremiah. For the very word which came to Jeremiah bears witness to him, saying: “Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you; and before you came forth from the vulva, I sanctified you and appointed you a prophet among the nations” (Jer. 1:5). But he was not a prophet among the nations. Therefore, since the word of God is true, it must present what it promised, so that he may be a prophet among the nations.

4. These are the two lampstands standing in the sight of the Lord of the earth. He spoke of these two lampstands and two olive trees and called attention to them so that, if you read the passage elsewhere and did not understand it, you might understand it here. For in Zechariah, one of the twelve prophets, it is written thus: “These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands which stand in the sight of the Lord of the earth” (Zech. 4:14), that is, they are in paradise.

Alternatively, in another sense: standing in the sight of the lord of the earth—that is, in the sight of Antichrist. These, therefore, must be killed by Antichrist.

7. And the beast which ascends from the abyss. After many plagues have been completed in the world, he says that at the end the beast ascends from the abyss. That it will ascend from the abyss is confirmed by many testimonies. For he says [Col. 0335A] in Ezekiel, chapter 31: “Behold Asshur, a cypress on Mount Lebanon” (Ezek. 31:3). “Asshur” means one who crushes; the tall, branch-covered cypress signifies a numerous people on Mount Lebanon, in the kingdom of kingdoms—that is, of the Romans. When he calls it beautiful in its shoots, he means mighty in its armies. “Water,” he says, “will nourish him”—that is, the many thousands of people who will be subjected to him. “And the abyss increased him”—that is, it belched him forth. Isaiah also speaks in almost the same words.

That he was in the Roman kingdom and was among the Caesars is also solemnly attested by the apostle Paul. For he says to the Thessalonians: “Let him who now restrains continue to restrain until he is taken out of the midst; and then the lawless one will appear, he whose coming is according to the activity of Satan, with lying signs and wonders” (2 Thess. 2:7–8). And so that they might know that the one who was then ruler would come, [Col. 0335B] he added: “The mystery of wickedness is already at work” (ibid., 9)—that is, he secretly contrives the wickedness which he is going to commit.

Yet he is not raised up by his own power, nor by that of his father, but by God’s command. Concerning this Paul says to the same people: “Therefore, because they did not receive the love of God, he will send them a spirit of error, so that all who have not been persuaded by the truth may be persuaded by the lie” (ibid., 10). And Isaiah says: “While they waited for light, darkness arose for them” (Isa. 59:9).

The Apocalypse therefore reveals that these prophets are killed by that same person and rise again on the fourth day, lest anyone be found equal to God.

8. And their bodies will lie in the streets of the great city which is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt. By Sodom and Egypt he means Jerusalem, which has become a heap of persecuting people.

It is therefore necessary to follow the prophetic proclamation attentively [Col. 0335C] and with the greatest care, and to understand that the Spirit both proclaims from the Father and reverses the order; and when he has run forward to the very end, he again repeats earlier times. What he will do once, he sometimes shows as though it had already happened. Unless you understand it sometimes as accomplished and sometimes as future, you will fall into profound darkness. The interpretation of the statements that follow has therefore shown that it is not the order of the reading but the meaning of the discourse that must be understood.

> **Note:** [Col. 0335D] *Reverses the order.* He uses the verb *praeposterat* for “sets in reverse order,” following a manner of speech peculiar to those times and perhaps also to his own nation. [Col. 0336D]

19. And the temple of God which is in heaven was opened. The opening of the temple is the manifestation of our Lord. For the Son is the temple of God, as he himself says: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I shall raise it up” (John 2:19–21). And when the Jews said, “This temple was built in forty-six [Col. 0335D] years,” he was speaking, the Evangelist says, of the temple of his body.

And the ark of the Lord’s covenant was seen in his temple. He says that the preaching of the Gospel, the remission of sins, and all the gifts whatsoever which came with him appeared.

## FROM CHAPTER XII

1–2. And a great sign was seen in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon beneath her feet, and upon her head [Col. 0336A] a crown of twelve stars; and having a child in her womb, she cried out in labor and endured torments in order to give birth.

The woman clothed with the sun, having the moon beneath her feet, wearing upon her head a crown of twelve stars, and laboring in her pains is the ancient Church of the patriarchs, prophets, saints, and apostles. She endured the groans and torments of her longing until she saw Christ—the fruit long ago promised to her from her people according to the flesh—take a body from that very nation.

Her being clothed with the sun signifies the hope of resurrection and the glory of the promise. The moon signifies the decline of the saints’ bodies under the debt of death, which can never fail. For just as life diminishes, so it also increases. Nor is the hope of those who sleep wholly extinguished, as some think; rather, they have [Col. 0336B] light in the darkness, like the moon. The crown of twelve stars signifies the choir of the patriarchs according to fleshly descent, from whom Christ was to take flesh.

3. And another sign was seen in heaven: behold, a red dragon having seven heads. When he says that it is red—that is, scarlet in color—the fruit of its works has given it such a color. For from the beginning it was, as the Lord says, a murderer; and it has oppressed the entire human race not only under the debt of death, but also by various swords and forms of destruction. The seven heads are seven Roman kings, from among whom Antichrist also comes, as we said earlier.

And ten horns. By these he means the same ten kings at the last time, as we shall discuss more fully there.

[Col. 0336C] 4. And his tail held a third part of the stars of heaven, and cast them to the earth. When he says that the dragon’s tail drew a third part of the stars of heaven, this can be understood in two ways. Many think that he will be able to seduce a third part of believing humanity. But what should more truly be understood is that, when he was still a prince and descended by his own determination, he seduced a third part of the angels subject to him. Thus the Apocalypse affirms what we said above.

And the dragon stood in the sight of the woman who was beginning to give birth, so that, when she had given birth, he might devour her son. The red dragon who stands and longs to devour the son as soon as she gives birth is the devil, namely the apostate angel, [Col. 0336D] who believed that the destruction of all human beings through death was alike. But he who was not born from seed owed nothing to death; therefore the dragon could not devour him—that is, detain him in death—for he rose on the third day. Indeed, even before he suffered, the devil approached to tempt him as though he were merely human; but when he found that he was not the one he had supposed, he departed from him until the appointed time. Hence it is said here:

5. And she gave birth to a son who begins to rule all nations with an iron rod. The iron rod is the sword of persecution.

[Col. 0337A] I saw all depart from their places. That is, the good will be moved, fleeing persecution.

And the son was caught up to God and to his throne. We also read in the Acts of the Apostles that he was caught up to the throne of God: while speaking with his disciples, he was caught up into heaven.

6. But the woman fled into the wilderness; and there were given to her the two wings of a great eagle. The aid of the wings of the great eagle—namely, the gift of the prophets—is given to that catholic Church from which, at the last time, 144,000 people will believe through the preaching of Elijah. But he also says here that the rest of the people will be found alive at the coming of the Lord. And the Lord says in the Gospel: “Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains” (Luke 21:21)—that is, let all who have been gathered in Judea [Col. 0337B] go to the place prepared for them and be nourished there for three years and six months away from the face of the devil.

14. The two great wings. These are the two prophets: Elijah and the prophet who will be with him.

15. And the serpent sent from his mouth after the woman water like a river, so that the river might carry her away. The water which the serpent sent from his mouth signifies the people who, at his command, persecute her.

16. And the earth helped the woman, and opened its mouth, and swallowed the river which the dragon sent from his mouth. The earth’s opening its mouth and devouring the waters reveals vengeance upon those then present.

Thus, although he signifies her as laboring in childbirth, he afterward shows her fleeing once the child has been born, because the two events did not occur at one time. For we know that Christ has been born; but time was to intervene before she fled from the face of the serpent, and this has not yet happened. [Col. 0337C] He then says:

7–9. There was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought with the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought; but they did not prevail, nor was their place found any longer in heaven. And that great dragon, the ancient serpent, was cast down; he was cast down to the earth. This is the beginning of Antichrist. Yet first Elijah must preach, and there must be a time of peace. Afterward, when the three years and six months of Elijah’s preaching have been completed, the devil too is to be cast down from heaven, where until that time he had possessed the power to ascend. And Paul the Apostle says that all the apostate angels, and likewise Antichrist, are to be raised from the underworld: “Unless the apostasy comes first, and the man of sin is revealed, the son of perdition and [Col. 0337D] the adversary, who exalts himself above everything called God or worshiped” (2 Thess. 2:3–4).

## FROM CHAPTER XIII

1. And I saw a beast like a leopard ascending from the sea. [Col. 0338A] It signifies the kingdom of Antichrist at that time, mingled with a diversity of nations and peoples.

2. His feet were like those of a bear. The bear is a powerful and exceedingly filthy beast. By the feet we should understand his leaders.

And his mouth was like a lion’s. That is, his mouth is armed for bloodshed: it signifies his command and tongue, which will go forth for nothing other than the shedding of blood.

### XVII, 9

The seven heads are seven mountains upon which the woman sits. That is, the Roman city.

> **Note:** [Col. 0337D] *The seven heads are seven mountains.* This is taken from chapter 17:9, as far as the point at which he again begins interpreting the words of chapter 13, when he says, “For it is the number of a man.” We were unwilling to alter these words because the interpreter himself says that the Holy Spirit does not preserve the order of the words, but sometimes passes from the last things back to the interpretation of the first.

10. And they are seven kings: five have fallen, one exists, and another has not yet come; and when he comes, he will remain for a short time. The time at which the written Apocalypse was published must be understood. Domitian was then Caesar; before him were his brother Titus, [Col. 0338B] Vespasian, Otho, Vitellius, and Galba. These are the five who have fallen. One exists—namely Domitian, under whom the Apocalypse was written. “Another has not yet come” means Nerva; and when he came, he remained a short time, for he did not complete two years.

> **Note:** [Col. 0337D] This is taken from chapter 17. —GALL.

11. And the beast which you saw is of the seven. For Nero reigned before these kings.

And it is the eighth. He now says:

> **Note:** [Col. 0337D] *He now says.* This passage tormented me for a long time, since it was shamefully corrupt, unless I am mistaken. I nevertheless attempted to correct it; whether I succeeded, more learned scholars will judge. In the manuscript it read thus: “He now says, when that one comes, cut off in the eighth place, because in it is the consummation. He says that Antichrist will come in the eighth place; for perfection is designated by the number eight. Since the end of the world will have come, he therefore adds: because in him is the consummation.” [Col. 0338D]

“When that one comes, count the eighth place, because in him is the consummation,” he added.

And he will go into destruction. For he says that ten kings receive royal power when that one sets out from the East: “He will be sent from the city of Rome with his armies.” Daniel reveals the ten horns and ten diadems. Three are to be uprooted from among the earlier kings—that is, three principal leaders [Col. 0338C] are to be killed by Antichrist. The remaining seven will give him honor, counsel, and power. Concerning them he says:

16. These will hate the harlot—that is, the city—and will burn her flesh with fire.

By the fact that one of the heads was as though slain unto death, and that its mortal wound was healed, he means Nero. For it is established that, when cavalry sent by the senate was pursuing him, he cut his own throat. God will therefore send him after he has been raised up, a fitting king—fitting, that is, for what the Jews have deserved.

And because he will bear one name but establish another, so that the Jews may receive him as Christ, Daniel says: “He will not know the desires of women” (Dan. 11:37), although previously he had been exceedingly impure, “and he will not know any God of his fathers.” For he will not be able to seduce the people of the circumcision unless he is an arbiter of the Law. Indeed, he will not recall the saints to the worship of idols, but to the reception of circumcision, and he will seduce whomever he can. For he will act in such a way as to be called Christ by them.

We have already said above, [Col. 0339A] on the authority of Isaiah’s words, that he rises from the underworld: “Water will nourish him, and the underworld increased him.” Nevertheless, although he comes with his name and conduct changed, the Spirit says:

> **Note:** [Col. 0338D] Here he returns to chapter 13. —GALL.

### XIII, 18

The number of his name is the number of a man, and his number is six hundred and sixty-six. Just as they calculate from Greek letters, so in many copies is found τεῖταν (*teitan*). For τεῖταν has this number; the Gentiles call the Sun and Phoebus by this name. In Greek it is calculated thus: τ, three hundred; ε, five; ι, ten; τ, three hundred; α, one; ν, fifty. Added together, these make six hundred and sixty-six. So far as the Greek letters are concerned, they complete this number and name.

> **Note:** [Col. 0339D] **TEITAN.** Here Victorinus imitates Irenaeus, *Against Heresies*, book V, chapter 30, §3—or, if you prefer, his disciple Hippolytus, *Demonstration concerning Christ and Antichrist*, chapter 50. See what we annotated on the cited passage of Hippolytus, volume II of the *Library of the Fathers*, p. 435. As for the following word **DICLVX**, I scarcely doubt that Nicholas of Lyra took it from our Victorinus in his *Perpetual Postils* on Revelation 13:18. On this matter Bossuet, the most learned bishop of Meaux, should be consulted, *On Revelation* 13:18. From this it is clear that our holy Father is reproached here somewhat incautiously by Millanius. —GAL.

If you wish to turn that name into Latin, it is understood by antiphrasis as **DICLVX**. Its letters are calculated in this way: D signifies five hundred; I, one; C, [Col. 0339B] one hundred; L, fifty; V, five; X, ten. When the letters are added together, this likewise makes six hundred and sixty-six—that is, what sounds in Greek as τεῖταν (*teitan*), namely what in Latin is called **DICLVX**.

> **Note:** [Col. 0339D] **DICLVX.** This sort of derivation or translation of the name demonstrates that this man was plainly ignorant of humane and refined literature. Indeed, this interpretation seemed so inept and unworthy of a learned man that one might readily suspect it had first been written in the margin by some unskilled person, and subsequently attached to the commentary by others still more unskilled, rather than handed down by the author. [Col. 0340D]

By this name, expressed through antiphrasis, we understand Antichrist, who, although cut off and deprived of the light above, nevertheless transforms himself into an angel of light and dares to call himself the light.

> **Note:** [Col. 0340D] *D signifies five hundred.* Here, as also shortly afterward in several places, the nominative remains in place of the accusative. The interpretation is certainly, in my judgment, feeble and trivial. Yet I preferred to leave it to be corrected by the judgment of the more learned rather than boldly determine anything about it myself.

Likewise, in a certain Greek codex we find ἀντεμος (*antemos*). When its letters are calculated, you will find the number as above: α, one; ν, fifty; τ, three hundred; ε, five; μ, forty; ο, seventy; ς, two hundred. Together these make six hundred and sixty-six according to the Greeks.

Likewise, another name of his in Gothic, which will be clear in itself, is γενσήρικος (*gensērikos*). You will calculate it in the same way by Greek letters: γ, three; ε, five; ν, fifty; σ, two hundred; η, [Col. 0339C] eight; ρ, one hundred; ι, ten; κ, twenty; ο, seventy; ς, again two hundred. These, as stated above, make six hundred and sixty-six.

11. And I saw another beast ascending from the earth. He means the great false prophet, who will perform signs, wonders, and falsehoods before Antichrist in the sight of humankind.

And it had two horns like a lamb—that is, inwardly the appearance of a man—and it spoke like a dragon. It is the devil, full of wickedness, who speaks. For it will do these things in the sight of humankind, so that even the dead may appear to rise.

13. And it will cause fire to descend from heaven in the sight of humankind. But, as I have said, only “in the sight of humankind.” Magicians accomplish these things through apostate angels even to the present day.

[Col. 0339D] It will also cause a golden image of Antichrist to be placed in the temple at Jerusalem. An apostate angel will enter it and from it issue voices and oracular responses. The false prophet himself will also cause slaves and free persons to receive on their foreheads or right hands the mark—the number of Antichrist’s name—so that no one may buy or sell.

Daniel foretold the object of abhorrence and the provocation of God (Dan. 11:45): “And he will establish,” he says, “his temple between Samaria and the illustrious and holy mountain”—that is, at Jerusalem—setting up an image as Nebuchadnezzar had done.

At that point he inserts the matter here; now, however, he recalls what the Lord said when warning his churches about the last times and their dangers: “But when you see the object of abhorrence spoken of through the prophet Daniel standing in the holy place—let the reader understand” (Matt. 24:15; Dan. 9:27).

It is called an “object of abhorrence” (*aspernatio*) when God is provoked, because idols are worshiped as God, or when the doctrine of heretics is introduced into the churches. An “aversion” (*aversio*) occurs when steadfast [Col. 0340B] people, seduced by false signs and wonders, turn away from salvation.

## FROM CHAPTER XIV

6. And I saw an angel flying through the midst of heaven. We have already discussed above the angel whom he says he saw flying through the midst of heaven: he is the same Elijah who, by his preaching, precedes the kingdom of Antichrist.

8. And another angel following him. By the other angel following him he means the prophet who is the companion of Elijah’s preaching. As for what he says:

15. Send forth your sharp sickle, and harvest the clusters of the vine. This signifies the nations that will perish at the coming of the Lord. He reveals this same thing under several figures, [Col. 0340C] as in the dry harvests and the seed: the coming of the Lord, the consummation of the world, the kingdom of Christ, and the future manifestation of the kingdom of the blessed.

19–20. And the angel sent forth the sickle, harvested the vine of the earth, and cast it into the winepress of the wrath of God; and the winepress of fury was trodden outside the city. When he says that it was cast into the winepress of God’s wrath and trodden outside the city, the treading of the winepress is the retribution of the sinner.

And blood came out of the winepress as far as the bridles of the horses. Vengeance for the blood that was shed will come forth, as was foretold earlier: “You sinned in blood, and blood will pursue you” (Ezek. 35:6).

For one thousand six hundred stadia. That is, through all four regions of the world; for fourfoldness is fourfolded, as in the four faces, the fourfold forms, and the square wheels. For four times four hundred is one thousand six hundred. The Apocalypse says this while repeating the same persecution.

## FROM CHAPTER XV

[Col. 0341A]

1. And I saw another great and marvelous sign: seven angels having the seven last plagues, because in them the indignation of God was consummated. For the wrath of God always strikes a contumacious people with seven plagues—that is, perfectly—as he says in Leviticus (Lev. 26:24). These will occur at the end, when the Church has departed from the midst.

2. Standing upon the glassy sea, having harps. That is, they stood steadfastly in the faith upon their baptism, having their confession in their mouths, and they will exult in the kingdom before God. But let us return to the matters proposed.

## FROM CHAPTER XVII
[Col. 0341B] 1, 6. And one of the seven angels who have the seven bowls came and spoke with me, saying: Come, I will show you the judgment of that great harlot who sits upon many waters. And I saw the woman drunk with the blood of the saints and the blood of the martyrs. The decrees of that senate of hers have always been carried out against everyone, in opposition to the preaching of the true faith. And now, after an indulgence has already been proclaimed, he himself too has issued a decree throughout all nations.

3. And I saw the woman herself sitting upon a scarlet beast, full of names of blasphemy. Her sitting upon the red beast—the author of murders—is an image of the devil; there too is the matter of his captivity, which we have discussed. I recall that this Babylon is so called because of confusion, both in the Apocalypse and in [Col. 0341C] Isaiah; and Ezekiel named it Sodom. Finally, if you compare what was said against Sodom, what Isaiah says against Babylon, and what the Apocalypse says, you will find that all of them are one and the same.

## FROM CHAPTER XIX

11. And I saw heaven opened; and behold, a white horse, and he who sat upon it was called Faithful and True. The horse and the one sitting upon it signify our Lord coming with the heavenly army to his kingdom. For from the northern sea, which is the Arabian Sea, as far as the Phoenician Sea and to the ends of the earth, they will command the greater parts of these regions at the coming of the Lord Jesus [reading uncertain].

> **Note:** [Col. 0341D] *At the coming of the Lord Jesus they will command.* What if, by changing only one letter, you were to read *they will cleanse*? Nor were we able to find any word more appropriate that, through the similarity of its syllables, [Col. 0342D] would cohere with what immediately follows.

And all the souls of the nations will be gathered for judgment.

## FROM CHAPTER XX

[Col. 0341D]

1–3. And I saw an angel descending from heaven, holding the key of the abyss and a chain in his hand. And he seized the dragon, that ancient serpent who is surnamed the devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years; and he cast him into the abyss, and shut it, and set a seal over him, so that he might no longer deceive the nations until the thousand years were ended. After these things he must be released for a short time. Those years during which Satan is bound are the years from the first coming of Christ until the end of the age. [Col. 0342A] They are called a thousand according to that manner of speaking in which a part is signified by the whole, as in the passage: “The word that he commanded for a thousand generations” (Ps. 104:8), although there are not a thousand.

As for the statement, “and he cast him into the abyss,” he says this because the devil, excluded from the hearts of believers, began to possess the impious, in whose blind hearts he is shut up every day as though in the depths of the abyss. “And he shut it,” he says, “and set a seal over him, so that he might not deceive the nations until the thousand years were ended.” It is said that he shut it over him—that is, he forbade and restrained him from deceiving those who belong to Christ. He set a seal over him because it is hidden who belong to the devil’s portion and who to Christ’s. For even of those who appear to stand, we do not know whether they will fall; and concerning those who lie fallen, it is uncertain whether they will rise.

As for [Col. 0342B] the statement that he was bound and shut up so that he might not deceive the nations: the nations signify the Church, which consists of them and which he previously held in deception, “until,” he says, “the thousand years are ended”—that is, what remains of the sixth day, namely, of the sixth age, which consists of a thousand years. “After these things he must be released for a short time.” The short time signifies three years and six months, during which the devil, under Antichrist, will exert all his strength in taking vengeance against the Church. He then says afterward that the devil will be released and will deceive the nations throughout the whole world, and will draw them into war against the Church; the number of those enemies will be like the sand of the sea.

4, 5. And I saw thrones and those sitting upon them, and judgment was given to them; and I saw the souls of those slain because of the testimony [Col. 0342C] of Jesus and because of the word of God, and those who had not worshiped the beast or its image, nor received the inscription upon their forehead or upon their hand; and they reigned with Jesus for a thousand years. The rest of them did not live again until the thousand years were ended. This is the first resurrection. There are two resurrections; but the first resurrection is now the resurrection of souls through faith, which does not permit human beings to pass into the second death. Of this resurrection the Apostle says: “If you have risen with Christ, seek the things that are above” (Col. 3:1).

6. Blessed and holy is the one who has a share in this resurrection. Over these the second death will have no power, but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and will reign with him for a thousand years. I do not think that the kingdom of a thousand years is eternal; or, if this is how it must be understood, [Col. 0342D] when the thousand years have been completed they cease to reign. But I shall set forth the matter as the capacity of my understanding apprehends it.

> **Note:** [Col. 0342D] *The kingdom of a thousand years.* Unless scruple about being led away from the author’s purpose prevented me, I would gladly have restored this passage as follows: “I think that the kingdom of a thousand years is eternal; or, if it must not be understood in this way,” etc. [Col. 0343C]

The number ten signifies the Decalogue, and the number one hundred represents the crown of virginity. For whoever has preserved intact the resolve of virginity, faithfully fulfilled the commandments of the Decalogue, and slain savage dispositions or impure thoughts within the chamber of the heart so that they may not rule over him—he is a true priest of Christ and, by completing the number one thousand, is rightly believed to reign with Christ; and in him the devil is rightly bound. [Col. 0343A] But in anyone entangled in vices and the doctrines of heretics, the devil is released. Yet because he says that the devil is released when the thousand years have been completed, and when the number of the perfect saints—in whom the glory of virginity exists in body and heart—has been completed, many, deceived by him through love of earthly things at the abominable coming of the kingdom that is to come [reading uncertain], will be overthrown and will enter the lake of fire together with him.

> **Note:** [Col. 0343D] *That is to come.* I think one should read *future* or *when it comes*.

8–10. And they went up over the breadth of the earth and surrounded the camp of the saints and the beloved city; and fire came down from heaven from God and consumed them. And the devil who deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and sulfur, where the beast and the false prophet also will be tormented day and night for ever and ever. [Col. 0343B] This now pertains to the Last Judgment. A little afterward the earth was rendered holy—the earth, certainly, in which their virginal bodies had long rested. With the immortal King they will receive an eternal kingdom: those who preserved themselves inviolably from wickedness, not only as virgins in body, but equally in speech and thought; They are shown to remain destined to rejoice with the Lamb.

> **Note:** [Col. 0343D] *Preserved.* I think this has been used in place of *have preserved themselves*. Since we had no better reading than the one we found in the old copy, we left it unchanged, even though it did not at all commend itself to us, so that more learned men might either accept our conjecture or correct at their own discretion this corrupted passage. I was unwilling to alter obsolete words, so that I might depart as little as possible from the ancient manuscript. [Col. 0344C] In these annotations I have supplied in good faith what I could safely correct; nor, if anyone rejects my opinion, will I immediately become angry with him, provided only that he offers a better and more certain one. So far am I from rejecting such an opinion that I shall sincerely profess myself its defender. Certainly the little book was so badly treated by scribes that it seemed scarcely possible to restore it even with every diligence. Hence we are less to be blamed if in some places we preferred to follow conjecture rather than the authority of a corrupted copy. [Col. 0344D]

## FROM CHAPTERS XXI AND XXII

16. And the city is laid out as a square. He says that the city is square, that it gleams with gold and precious stones, and that it has a holy street, a river running through its midst, and the tree of life on either side, producing twelve fruits during the twelve months; that the light of the sun is not there because the Lamb is its light; that [Col. 0343C] its gates are each made from a single pearl, with three gates on each of the four sides; and that they cannot be shut.

The square city, I say, represents the united multitude of the saints, in whom faith could in no way waver. Just as Noah is commanded (Gen. 6:14) to make the ark from squared timbers, so that it might withstand the violence of the flood, the precious stones, which cannot waver under persecution, represent holy men who could neither be shaken by the tempest of persecutors nor [Col. 0344A] be separated from the true faith by the force of the rain. They are therefore joined to pure gold, and from them the city of the great King is adorned.

Their streets represent hearts cleansed of all defilements and radiant with transparent light, so that the Lord may worthily walk in them. The river of life represents the grace of spiritual teaching flowing through the minds of the faithful and causing manifold, fragrant vegetation to spring forth. The tree of life on either bank represents Christ’s coming according to the flesh: receiving life from the one tree of the cross, he satisfied peoples consumed by hunger through the preaching of the word of God.

And because he says that the sun is not needed in the city, he clearly shows that the Creator shines in its midst as an immaculate light, whose brilliance no faculty has been able [Col. 0344B] to conceive and no tongue to express.

As for his statement that three gates, each made from a single pearl, are set on each of the four sides, I think that the four are the virtues—namely prudence, courage, justice, and temperance—which adhere to one another. And when they are mutually combined, they make the number twelve. We believe that the twelve gates are the number of the Apostles. Shining like precious pearls in the four virtues and manifesting among the saints the light of their teaching, they enable people to enter the heavenly city, so that the choir of angels may rejoice over their manner of life.

That the gates cannot be shut clearly shows that no tempest raised by opponents can separate the Apostles’ teaching from rectitude, even if the surging masses of the nations and the vain superstitions of heretics [Col. 0344C] rise against their true faith. Once defeated, they will dissolve like foam, because Christ is the rock by whom and through whom the Church is founded. Therefore it is overcome by no waves of raging human beings.

Consequently, those who assert that the thousand-year kingdom is earthly, and who agree with the heretic Cerinthus, must not be heard. For the kingdom of Christ is now everlasting in the saints, when the glory of the saints has been manifested after the resurrection.

# THE COMPLETE WORKS OF MAGNES THE PRESBYTER

[Col. 0343]

# HISTORICAL NOTICE CONCERNING MAGNES THE PRESBYTER, WITH A FRAGMENT

## TAKEN FROM D. LUMPER

## ARTICLE I. A Summary of His Life

[Col. 0343D]

### The period in which Magnes, also called Macarius Magnes, flourished. He is said to have been a presbyter of Jerusalem. Was he also a bishop?

Magnes—or Magnetes, or rather Macarius Magnes—is thought to have flourished at the close of the third century. [Col. 0344D] This is the view above all of the most learned Tillemont, who discusses this writer of the Church, though his name is obscure, and his literary remains with sufficient care. [Col. 0345A]

> **Note:** [Col. 0345D] Tillemont, *Mémoires*, or *Histoire des Empereurs*, vol. IV, pp. 308–311, in the *Life of Constantine the Great*, art. XCIII, Brussels ed., p. 127 ff.

William Cave, however, declares that at last he was able to discover not only the author’s previously unknown period, but also the rank with which he was distinguished. For he writes as follows:

> **Note:** [Col. 0345D] Cave, *Historia litteraria*, at the year 265, vol. I, p. 136.

Germanus, patriarch of Constantinople, in a manuscript *Dogmaticus addressed to Anthimus* held by the distinguished Gale, where he deals with the Antiochene synod against the Samosatene, has the following:

“Present,” he says, “at the Council of Antioch against Paul of Samosata were Gregory Thaumaturgus, Leo of Tarsus”—according to Cave’s judgment, one should read Ἕλενος, “Helenus,” instead of Λέων, “Leo,” with a slight alteration, for Helenus was bishop of Tarsus at that time, as [Col. 0345B] Eusebius, Syncellus, and Nicephorus expressly state—“Maximus of Bostra, and a certain Magnes, a priest of Jerusalem, and Firmilian the Admirable of our Cappadocia” (καὶ Ἱεροσολύμων Μάγνης τις ἱερεὺς καὶ τῆς ἡμετέρας Καππαδοκίας Φιρμιλιανὸς ὁ Θαμάσιος), Theotecnus, Photinus, Marcellus, etc.

He therefore flourished in the year 265, when the synod against Paul was held at Antioch, or at least in one of the following two years. For Eusebius, book VII, chapter 28, reports that the bishops assembled “at various times, in different ways, and frequently” (κατὰ καιρὸν διαφόρως καὶ πολλάκις). This must be understood either of different synods or of different sessions of the same synod. Whatever the case, Germanus can scarcely be understood as referring to any synod other than the one held in 265, since Gregory Thaumaturgus is said to have died about that year.

Since, therefore, our Magnes was a priest of Jerusalem, he accompanied his bishop Hymenaeus to it. For several presbyters [Col. 0345C] and deacons attended this council. Thus far Cave.

### On the literary remains of Magnes himself

As regards Magnes’ presbyteral rank, however, it must be observed with Tillemont that his name was prefaced by the title “bishop” (ἱεράρχης, “hierarch”) in the copy of the work committed to writing by him that was discovered near the beginning of the ninth century by the orthodox who were contending with the Iconoclasts.

Photius relates:

> **Note:** [Col. 0345D] Photius, *Bibliotheca*, cod. LIX.

As Le Quien notes:

> **Note:** [Col. 0345D] Le Quien, *Oriens Christianus*, vol. II, p. 698. Not a single word about Magnes occurs in this passage; Gallandi’s citation is false. These things, however, are found in note 5.

Among the prelates who assembled against Chrysostom at the Synod of the Oak, a suburb of Chalcedon, there also stood Macarius of Magnesia, or bishop of the Magnetes, the accuser of Heraclides, whom Chrysostom himself had created bishop of Ephesus. From this circumstance perhaps, whether through fraud or ignorance, a copyist added the title of bishop when transcribing the work of the earlier Magnes. [Col. 0345D]

### The five books of *Responses against Theosthenes*, very well known in the age of Damascene

However that may be, Macarius Magnes wrote five books of *Apocritics* (Ἀποκριτικά), or *Responses*, against the pagan Theosthenes, who was maligning the Gospel. The Le Quien just praised noted that these books were very well known in the age of Damascene. [Col. 0346A]

> **Note:** [Col. 0346D] Vol. I, p. 271, of the works of St. Damascene. Le Quien, in the notes on the works of Damascene, vol. I, p. 271.

Many excerpts (ἀποσπασμάτια) from these same *Apocritics* are known to survive in the *Antirrhetic Books against the Iconoclasts* of Nicephorus, patriarch of Constantinople. At the beginning of this century the distinguished Anselmo Banduri, a Benedictine monk and abbot, transcribed them from the royal manuscripts and had all but promised learned men that he would publish them.

> **Note:** [Col. 0346D] Fabricius, *Bibliotheca Graeca*, vol. V, pp. 641–683.

To them were also to be added several fragments of a commentary on Genesis by the same Macarius Magnes, taken from an Ottobonian manuscript.

Even earlier, the most learned Jean Boivin had discovered in the *Antirrhetics* of Nicephorus a complete book of excerpts from our writer’s *Apocritics*, entitled *On the Testimonies of Macarius Magnes*, as he himself attests.

> **Note:** [Col. 0346D] Boivin, in the notes on Nicephorus Gregoras, p. 794.

[Col. 0346B] While we were eagerly awaiting the publication by these two eminent men of such precious remains of this most ancient writer, Magnus Crusius subsequently gave us hope that we would soon receive from him the same excerpts, which Boivin himself had communicated to him.

> **Note:** [Col. 0346D] Crusius, *Dissertatio Epistolica*, § II, pp. 8–11.

They were taken, he says, from book IV of the *Apocritics*, in which the author, in order to establish the truth of the Christian religion, argues chiefly against a certain Greek philosopher; in particular, he discusses the divine monarchy and its majesty against the idolatry of the pagans.

He adds: “To this work will also be appended fragments of the commentary on Genesis by the same Macarius Magnes. In them he discusses the creation of Adam, the blessing of the seventh day, the planting of the garden of Eden, Adam’s assignment of names to each kind [Col. 0346C] of beast, the help of the woman instituted by God himself, the serpent’s deception and the fall of the first parents, and finally the garments of skin fashioned by God.” Thus far the distinguished Crusius.

Would that either the complete work of Macarius Magnes’ *Apocritics*, or at least excerpts from it, might someday appear in Greek and Latin.

### A fragment of Magnes concerning the Eucharist, formerly published by Turrianus and republished by Gallandi

Francisco Torres is indeed reported to have had that complete work in his hands. From it he extracted many passages here and there with which to defend the chief articles of the faith against the innovators. Above all, the learned man used it in his treatise on the Most Holy Eucharist, which he published against the Pole Andrzej Wolan, a disciple of Calvin. There he presents a most explicit testimony of Magnes concerning the real presence of the body and blood of Christ in the Eucharistic sacrament of the altar, taken from book III of his *Apocritics*. [Col. 0346D]

The indefatigable Andrea Gallandi had this passage transcribed from the first Florentine edition of that treatise, published in 1575, and printed in volume III of the *Library of the Ancient Fathers*, pp. 541–542—and rightly so, for the Paris edition of 1577, from which Fabricius drew and published it, [Col. 0347A] is found to be less correct.

> **Note:** [Col. 0347D] Fabricius, *Delectus Argumentorum*, pp. 70–72.

The new editor Gallandi further appended certain Greek passages presented by Allatius in his *Exercises against Creyghton*:

> **Note:** [Col. 0347D] Allatius, *Against Creyghton*, p. 563.

He also added the material produced by Zacharias of Crete in his *Responses to Guise, Cardinal of Lorraine*:

> **Note:** [Col. 0347D] Zacharias of Crete, *Responses*, p. 77.

These had not long before been published by Giovanni Lami:

> **Note:** [Col. 0347D] Lami, on Nicetas’ exposition of the First Epistle to the Corinthians, part I, p. 72 ff.

Finally, Gallandi thought it worthwhile to bring forward in his prolegomena, chapter XIII, p. 34, certain other passages cited from the same Magnes by the aforementioned Turrianus in his books in defense of the Epistles of the Popes, which Gallandi discovered at a later date. He did this so that none of the published fragments of this extremely ancient ecclesiastical writer might appear to be lacking from his collection of the ancient Fathers, until the *Antirrhetic Books against the Iconoclasts* of Nicephorus of Constantinople should emerge from some source; from these, many more excerpts from our Magnes will become available for the defense and adornment of the Church. [Col. 0347B]

The following are the passages:

“Magnetes,” says Turrianus—

> **Note:** [Col. 0347D] Turrianus, *Epistles of the Pontiffs and Apostolic Canons against the Magdeburg Centuriators*, Cologne, 1573, book I, chap. 5, p. 21.

—“a most ancient author, in book III of his *Apologetic against Theosthenes*, says:

> ‘Some victims,’ he says, ‘were slaughtered for the spirits of the air, others for earthly spirits, and others for subterranean spirits. Birds were sacrificed to the spirits of the air; to the ἐπιχθόνιοι, that is, the earthly spirits, black quadrupeds, because earth is black by nature; and to the ὑποχθόνιοι, that is, the subterranean spirits, likewise black quadrupeds in trenches or pits.’”

Thus far Magnetes.

And below:
